requirements.requirement: Operate infra.test authoritatively with node1 as primary, node2 and node3 as secondaries, app.infra.test resolving to node1's service address, and status.infra.test returning TXT ready.
requirements.summary: Runtime zone status identifies node1 as primary and node2/node3 as secondaries. All three were active, enabled, synchronized at served serial 2026090106, and returned authoritative AA answers for app=10.100.145.10 and status=ready; 10.100.145.10 is node1's observed address.

requirements.requirement: Serve infra.test as a DNSSEC-signed zone.
requirements.summary: The final signed zone passed dnssec-verify for ECDSAP256SHA256, and direct authoritative queries to the primary and both secondaries returned DNSKEY/RRSIG-signed data.

requirements.requirement: Support authenticated updates from node1 and propagate resulting changes to both secondaries.
requirements.summary: An unsigned update was refused and absent. A TSIG-authenticated update advanced the serial, appeared with an RRSIG on both secondaries, and its authenticated cleanup subsequently propagated to both at serial 2026090106.

requirements.requirement: Configure node4 to resolve through both node2 and node3.
requirements.summary: Node4's persistent NetworkManager profile and active resolv.conf list both secondary addresses. Direct queries through each returned the required records, and normal resolver-path queries succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Keep node4 DNS resolution available while one authoritative server is unavailable and restore healthy service afterward.
requirements.summary: The captured transition shows a healthy baseline through node2, node2 stopped with no port-53 listener and failed direct queries, successful node4 resolution through node3 during the outage, restoration of node2 at the current serial, and healthy resolution through both secondaries afterward.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence, including authenticated update propagation and the complete baseline-disruption-restoration sequence for resolver failover. The only observed defect is minor temporary-file residue on node1.
limitations: The bounded outage test disrupted node2 only; node1 and node3 outage cases were not independently exercised.
No reboot was captured, so persistence is evidenced by enabled services and node4's persistent NetworkManager profile rather than a reboot transition.
Lifecycle filesystem and socket observations are bounded inventories rather than exhaustive system audits.

operational_hygiene.summary: The final snapshots show no failed services or package-manager inconsistency, and the added DNS listeners are required by the task. Hygiene is slightly reduced because node1 retained /tmp/infra.test.db after an aborted staging command; it was absent from the baseline and appears to be an abandoned temporary zone-file copy.
